media.alt: The Context Introduction stage of the course 'Crafting Insightful Reports'. Above, the stage tabs: Pre-Class Prediction and Context Introduction ticked, then Interactive Challenge, Reinforcement Practice, Case Conference, and Core Concept Review. Below, a visual-novel scene in a school psychologist's office, where Dr. Reyes, supervising school psychologist, says: 'Keep that in mind as we go. Next, we will look closely at what each source actually says.' A case note reads: 'A report starts with its purpose and its audience.'
media.heading: Jordan visual novel
media.caption: Context Introduction. Dr. Reyes takes the student through Jordan's case one note at a time; all four case notes have been read here. Full size ↗

media.alt: The 'Connect the evidence' board. Six clue cards from the referral, Jordan, Jordan's teacher, and Jordan's parent are pinned to a board and joined in pairs with red string. All three patterns are found: reading takes longer than expected, understanding may be a relative strength, and difficulties show up around timed tasks. The feedback notes that the sources point to the same situation but do not show that anxiety causes the slowdown.
media.heading: Evidence board
media.caption: All three patterns found. Each one joins two clues from different sources, and the feedback separates agreement from cause. Full size ↗

media.alt: The 'Improve Jordan's report' activity, in three parts: check the draft against the report checklist, revise the weak sentences, then build a recommendation. On the left, the numbered sentences of Dr. Reyes's draft assessment report, each highlighted in a colour. On the right, the report checklist, with demographic information matched to sentence 1, cultural, linguistic and socioeconomic background marked missing, and the referral concern matched to sentence 2. 15 of 15 checklist items are resolved.
media.heading: Report & reflection
media.caption: The checklist stage, completed. Each draft sentence is matched to the checklist item it covers, and items the draft leaves out are marked as missing, not yet available, or not applicable. Full size ↗

media.alt: An annotated sketch of the kit as an open, cocoa-shell-shaped case. The lid holds the instructions; the base holds a wax-coated, bio-friendly package of cacao nibs, chocolate pieces and protein powder, paper molds, a spoon, and a bowl. The two halves are joined with cotton threads.

media.heading: Design

media.heading: Physical prototype
media.caption: Prototype 1, opened, with the kit's paper mold, wooden spoon, stirrer, and ingredient pouch inside.

media.alt: An illustrated instruction sheet. Safety warnings: adult supervision required, adults handle hot water and melting, the shell, paper molds, packaging and wooden spoon are not edible, the shell must not touch food, check allergens, and wash hands. Kit contents: a small paper bowl, chocolate paper molds, chocolate pieces, cacao nibs, protein powder, and a small wooden spoon, plus what you also need. Below, a six-step quest map: Prepare, Melt, Mix, Shape, Cool, and Enjoy, each marked as an adult step, a child step, or both.
media.heading: Instructions
media.caption: Prototype instruction sheet 1: safety, kit contents, and the six-step chocolate quest. Full size ↗

media.alt: The second instruction sheet. A sample nutrition facts panel with ingredients and allergens; three chocolate facts: cocoa pods hold cocoa beans, cocoa beans are used to make chocolate, and the cocoa pod husk is a big by-product once the pod is opened; and a bonus quest, 'Reuse the Shell', suggesting the shell as a seed starter or a treasure holder.
media.heading: Instructions
media.caption: Prototype instruction sheet 2: product information, cocoa facts, and the bonus quest to give the shell a second life. The nutrition panel is a layout sample, and the best-before and storage fields are placeholders, not product data. Full size ↗
